title: Maximum Product of Splitted Binary Tree
summary: Given a binary tree, determine the maximum product of the sums of two resulting subtrees after removing one edge.
statement: Given a binary tree, determine the maximum product of the sums of two resulting subtrees after removing one edge. Return this product modulo 10^9 + 7, ensuring the product is maximized before applying the modulo operation.
constraints: root contains at least two positive-valued nodes.
Remove exactly one edge, multiply the sums of the two resulting components, and maximize before applying modulo 1000000007.

After finding the total, each nonroot subtree defines one edge split with product sub*(total-sub).
Maximize the unmodded products and apply the modulus only once afterward.
Every removable parent edge corresponds uniquely to its child subtree sum, so all and only valid splits are tested.
editorial: One postorder traversal records every subtree sum and the root total. Removing the edge above any nonroot subtree yields exactly that sum and its complement, so maximize their product. Delaying the modulus preserves ordering. The oracle builds a separate tree and independently records component sums.
